decisions.title: Pages concurrency key split by ref allows overlapping deployments
decisions.reason: The diff definitely changes the concurrency semantics (group now keyed on github.ref; cancel-in-progress flipped false→true), but the headline failure scenario requires that the same workflow is triggered from two different refs, and the patch only shows lines 23-30 — no `on:` triggers are visible, so it cannot be established that any ref other than the deploy branch (e.g. refs/heads/main) ever runs this workflow. For the normal push-to-main path, github.ref is a constant, so the ref-suffixed group behaves like the old shared `pages` group and the 'different refs bypass mutual exclusion' claim does not follow from the changed lines alone. The one change that is unambiguously evidenced is `cancel-in-progress: true`, which can kill an in-flight `deploy` job on a rapid second push to the same ref; however the resulting impact is a transient failed deploy rather than a persistent bad state, because the superseding run then publishes the newest artifact — contradicting the 'site left stale' part of the scenario. Neither the conflicting `actions/deploy-pages` race (needs multi-ref or PR-triggered deploys) nor a sustained stale site is demonstrable from the supplied hunk, so I cannot confirm the described failure scenario nor fully dismiss the underlying concurrency-hygiene concern.
